primary_claim: In a randomized controlled trial, allowing experienced open-source developers to use early-2025 AI tools made them 19% slower at completing real repository issues, even though developers had forecast a 24% speedup and still believed afterward that AI had sped them up by 20%.

effect.value: 19% longer with AI allowed vs disallowed

contradicts_or_qualifies: Developers' own forecasts that AI would speed them up by 24%, and their post-hoc belief that AI had sped them up by 20%
Impressive AI performance on coding/agentic benchmarks such as SWE-Bench Verified and RE-Bench, and anecdotal reports of AI usefulness
stated_future_work: Run similar versions of this study in the future to track trends in speedup or slowdown from AI over time
Explore running experiments like this in other settings/companies
limitations_stated: Does not provide evidence that AI systems do not currently speed up many or most software developers, since the sample doesn't represent a majority of software development work
Only studies software development, not other domains
Does not claim near-future AI systems won't speed up developers in this exact setting
Does not claim there aren't ways of using existing AI systems more effectively (e.g. better prompting/scaffolding/finetuning) to achieve positive speedup
quote: When developers are allowed to use AI tools, they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts.
